_note: REACHED LIVE at :5050 — CmdK, then the board's own query, 'review'. The
`wait 400` before the keys is load-bearing: the input focuses on a 30ms
timeout, and keys pressed before it land on the document, which reads as an
unfiltered palette rather than a failed step.
WHAT THIS BOARD ACTUALLY DRAWS, and why the recipe drives 'review' rather
than an empty query: 303:1978 is named 'recent', but the frame draws the
RESULTS state — a typed query, an ACTIONS strip and a GO TO strip. The word
'recent' appears only in 333:2338, an ANNOTATION badge: absolutely
positioned at left 16 / top 16, i.e. ON TOP of the query row's own text at
left 20 / top 17, in a gray-200 pill with a gray-400 border. Two strings
cannot occupy one line; it is a sticky note on the board, not a control, and
is not joined. The RECENT strip itself is drawn by 166:2 and is measured
there (cmdk-band-recent, 220:927).
THIS BOARD IS THE ADJUDICATOR FOR STRIP ORDER, and the code moved to it.
166:27 draws the identical query, rows and strips but labels BOTH strips
'GO TO', which no grouped list can mean, so that frame cannot settle its own
order. This one labels them ACTIONS then GO TO and files the actions under
ACTIONS. Live banded in buildCommands' emission order, which put GO TO first
only because the navigation commands are pushed first;
shell/modals/CommandPalette.tsx now renders a fixed Recent · Suggested ·
Actions · Go to. The arrow keys walk the flattened banded list now too — a
render-only reorder would have left ArrowDown stepping between strips.
BOARD WON. It moves 166:27 and 166:2 as well as this one.
SAMPLE DATA, not conformed literally: the board's four rows are review-
workflow commands ('Send for review', 'Versions'), which the command
registry does not carry. Live 'review' returns one row per strip —
'Preview' (view-preview, ⌘+P) under ACTIONS and 'Open Review panel'
(nav-review, chord R, the board's own row and chord) under GO TO. Two
strips, each heading a chorded row, is the shape.
ALSO CHANGED, same file, same five boards: the rows were chrome-ui <Button>
with no variant, i.e. flowbite PRIMARY, so `enabled:hover:bg-primary-800`
survived the `tw:bg-*` override and the row under the pointer painted
#1E429F beneath a 13px --bk-ink label — 1.97:1, measured. Now
`variant="ghost"`. Full account in cmdk-empty's recipe.
NOT JOINED — I303:1981;16:17 and I303:1987;16:17, the strip LABELS. The
board colours them --color/ink-muted; live is --bk-ink-soft deliberately,
because 11px ink-muted on bg-subtle measures 4.39:1 (axe flagged 6 nodes)
and the component's own comment records it as open decision #1 in
FIGMA-TO-CODE/OPEN-DECISIONS.md — a Figma-side fix, not a call-site one.
Size and leading already match; only the colour is held open. The strip BOX
(28 tall, 16 gutters, 8 gap, bg-subtle tint) IS joined and passes.
ALSO NOT JOINED — 303:1984 and 303:1990's left-[580px] and every other
absolute horizontal number on a CmdK frame. 166:2's frame name records the
founder's own reading: '640x420 is chrome-ui/CommandPalette.tsx, which has
no importer; the shipping palette is 560 wide
(shell/modals/CommandPalette.tsx:388, tw:w-140).' The boards are drawn in
640-space against a component nothing imports, so their x-coordinates do not
transfer and the palette is NOT to be widened. Heights, type and fills all do
transfer, and those are what this recipe joins.
CONTRAST, REPORTED NOT HIDDEN — 4.38:1 on '⌘+P': --bk-ink-muted #6B7280 on
the selected row's --bk-accent-tint #EBF5FF at 11px. Same pair as cmdk-empty,
cmdk-typing, cmdk-results and pages-command-palette-k. The chord colour is
303:1984's own and diff compares it; the tint under it belongs to no board —
no CmdK frame draws a selected row at all. Recorded as a named pair so a NEW
failing pair still fails the run.
